+
+## Abstract
+
+For every positive j, the source caterpillars (5,j,j,4,3) and (4,j,j,5,3) have different second and identical third ordinary chromatic symmetric principal specializations.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Positive parts).**
+
+$$\forall (l : \mathbb{N}), \operatorname{Parts}\left(l\right) = (\operatorname{Fin}\left(l\right) \to \mathbb{N}^{+})$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/PrincipalSpecialization/BinghamCaterpillarPs3Family.Parts` (`✓ std3`).

+
+*Acknowledgement.* Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, and Mary Claire Simone (2026). *Principal specializations of the t-chromatic symmetric function*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A length-l composition is represented by a function from Fin l to the positive naturals. Fin l uses indices 0 through l−1. The source uses indices 1 through l; adding one identifies the spine indices.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The source vertex carrier).**
+
+$$\forall (l : \mathbb{N}), \forall (a : \operatorname{Parts}\left(l\right)), \operatorname{Vertex}\left(a\right) = \Sigma_{i:\operatorname{Fin}\left(l\right)} \operatorname{Fin}\left(\operatorname{PNat.val}\left(\operatorname{a}\left(i\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/PrincipalSpecialization/BinghamCaterpillarPs3Family.Vertex` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, and Mary Claire Simone (2026). *Principal specializations of the t-chromatic symmetric function*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The dependent pair (i,0) represents the source spine vertex v_(i+1). The pair (i,r), for 1 ≤ r < val(a(i)), represents its leaf w_(i+1,r). Thus the ith block has exactly val(a(i)) vertices. A part equal to one has no leaves.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The oriented source edge list).**
+
+$$\forall (l : \mathbb{N}), \forall (a : \operatorname{Parts}\left(l\right)), \forall (u : \operatorname{Vertex}\left(a\right)), \forall (v : \operatorname{Vertex}\left(a\right)), \operatorname{edgeRel}\left(a, u, v\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(((u_{1} = v_{1}) \land ((\operatorname{Fin.val}\left(u_{2}\right) = 0) \land (\operatorname{Fin.val}\left(v_{2}\right) \ne 0))) \lor ((\operatorname{Fin.val}\left(u_{2}\right) = 0) \land ((\operatorname{Fin.val}\left(v_{2}\right) = 0) \land (\operatorname{Fin.val}\left(u_{1}\right) + 1 = \operatorname{Fin.val}\left(v_{1}\right))))\right)$$

+*Source.* Repository-derived.

DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.
+

+
+Subscripts 1 and 2 denote the two projections of a vertex. The first disjunct lists spine-to-leaf edges inside a block; the second lists forward consecutive spine edges. The val maps are the natural-number projections of Fin elements.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The caterpillar).**
+
+$$\forall (l : \mathbb{N}), \forall (a : \operatorname{Parts}\left(l\right)), \operatorname{caterpillar}\left(a\right) = \operatorname{SimpleGraph.fromRel}\left(\operatorname{edgeRel}\left(a\right)\right)$$

DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.
+

+Mathlib SimpleGraph.fromRel symmetrizes the displayed relation and excludes loops. This is exactly Definition 2.1's caterpillar whenever the source endpoint conditions hold. Both five-part families satisfy those conditions for every positive j. The definition is total on all positive part vectors.

DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.

+Equation (2.1) of the source changes to colors 0 through k−1. SimpleGraph.Coloring means every edge has different endpoint colors; it imposes no surjectivity. Every proper coloring into Fin k occurs once in the finite sum. X is Polynomial.X over the integers. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.

+

DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.31785). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31785v1>.

+
+The domain is all positive integers, including j=1. Equality is formal polynomial equality in Z[X], with an indeterminate X. The second question, whether these are the only such pairs, is outside this statement.

+**Theorem 1.9 (The entire positive-parameter family).**
+
+$$\forall (j : \mathbb{N}^{+}), (\operatorname{ps}\left(\operatorname{caterpillar}\left(\operatorname{alpha}\left(j\right)\right), 2\right) \ne \operatorname{ps}\left(\operatorname{caterpillar}\left(\operatorname{beta}\left(j\right)\right), 2\right)) \land (\operatorname{ps}\left(\operatorname{caterpillar}\left(\operatorname{alpha}\left(j\right)\right), 3\right) = \operatorname{ps}\left(\operatorname{caterpillar}\left(\operatorname{beta}\left(j\right)\right), 3\right))$$

+# Integer bc ghost CAR
+
+## Abstract
+
+All integer bc ghost modes act on the algebraic countable finite-excitation carrier with the exact mixed delta, vacuum cuts, odd parity, a one-dimensional common annihilator kernel and scalar commutant.
+
+Fock, its signed creators and annihilators, vacuum and parity are those of CountableOccupationFock. Even sites encode the b-creator and c-annihilator pair; odd sites encode the c-creator and b-annihilator pair. Int.toNat is applied to a nonnegative expression in every active branch. CAR is transferred from the original finite Jordan–Wigner matrices through the proved occupation intertwinings and exact finite capture, then consumed by the exhaustive integer branch calculation.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (b).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Int,\; \operatorname{b}\left(m\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(m \le -2, \operatorname{create}\left(2 \cdot \operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{toNat}\left(-m - 2\right)\right), \operatorname{annihilate}\left(2 \cdot \operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{toNat}\left(m + 1\right) + 1\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.b` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The creation branch ends at m equal to minus two; the annihilation branch starts at minus one.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (c).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Int,\; \operatorname{c}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(n \le 1, \operatorname{create}\left(2 \cdot \operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{toNat}\left(1 - n\right) + 1\right), \operatorname{annihilate}\left(2 \cdot \operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{toNat}\left(n - 2\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.c` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The creation branch ends at n equal to one; the annihilation branch starts at two.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (mode correspondence).**
+
+$$\forall j \in Nat,\; \operatorname{b}\left(-\operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{ofNat}\left(j\right) - 2\right) = \operatorname{create}\left(2 \cdot j\right) \land \left(\operatorname{c}\left(\operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{ofNat}\left(j\right) + 2\right) = \operatorname{annihilate}\left(2 \cdot j\right) \land \left(\operatorname{c}\left(1 - \operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{ofNat}\left(j\right)\right) = \operatorname{create}\left(2 \cdot j + 1\right) \land \operatorname{b}\left(\operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{ofNat}\left(j\right) - 1\right) = \operatorname{annihilate}\left(2 \cdot j + 1\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.mode_correspondence` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+These four inverse formulas cover every natural occupation index and establish the zero-mode convention.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (ghost b car).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Int,\; \forall n \in Int,\; \operatorname{b}\left(m\right) \cdot \operatorname{b}\left(n\right) + \operatorname{b}\left(n\right) \cdot \operatorname{b}\left(m\right) = 0$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.ghost_b_car` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Same-species b modes anticommute. Cross-branch occupation indices have distinct parity.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (ghost c car).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Int,\; \forall n \in Int,\; \operatorname{c}\left(m\right) \cdot \operatorname{c}\left(n\right) + \operatorname{c}\left(n\right) \cdot \operatorname{c}\left(m\right) = 0$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.ghost_c_car` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Same-species c modes anticommute for the same exhaustive branch reason.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (ghost mixed car).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Int,\; \forall n \in Int,\; \operatorname{b}\left(m\right) \cdot \operatorname{c}\left(n\right) + \operatorname{c}\left(n\right) \cdot \operatorname{b}\left(m\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(m + n = 0, (1:\operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{End}\left(Complex, Fock\right)), 0\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Fermionic/BcGhostFock.ghost_mixed_car` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Only an even creator with its even annihilator, or an odd annihilator with its odd creator, contributes. In either case equality of occupation indices is equivalent to m plus n equal to zero. In particular the mixed zero-mode anticommutator is the identity.
+

+    cases b

+    · exact jw_create_intertwining N j _

+  · simpa [finiteMode] using finite_ac i j
+  · simpa [finiteMode, eq_comm, add_comm] using finite_ac j i

+    intro v _
+    exact hall v
+  intro v
+  induction v using Finsupp.induction_linear with

+      Submodule.subset_span ⟨w, rfl⟩
+    have he : Finsupp.single S a = (a / z) • (z • ket S) := by
+      rw [smul_smul, div_mul_cancel₀ _ hz]
+      simp [ket]
+    rw [he, ← hw]
+    exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ hword

+private theorem annihilate_coefficient (j : ℕ) (v : Fock) (S : Finset ℕ) (hj : j ∈ S) :

+  classical
+  induction v using Finsupp.induction_linear with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add f g hf hg =>
+    simp only [map_add, Finsupp.add_apply, hf, hg]
+    ring
+  | single T a =>
+    have hs : Finsupp.single T a = a • ket T := by simp [ket]
+    rw [hs, map_smul, annihilate_ket]
+    by_cases hjT : j ∈ T
+    · rw [if_pos hjT]

+      · subst T
+        simp [ket, smul_smul, mul_comm]

+          intro he
+          apply hTS
+          calc
+            T = insert j (T.erase j) := (Finset.insert_erase hjT).symm
+            _ = insert j (S.erase j) := congrArg (insert j) he
+            _ = S := Finset.insert_erase hj
+        simp [ket, he, hTS, eq_comm]
+    · have hTS : T ≠ S := by rintro rfl; exact hjT hj
+      simp [hjT, ket, hTS, eq_comm]
+
+/-- The simultaneous kernel of all actual annihilators is precisely the vacuum line. -/
+theorem common_annihilator_kernel (v : Fock) :
+    (∀ j : ℕ, annihilate j v = 0) ↔ ∃ α : ℂ, v = α • vacuum := by
+  classical
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    refine ⟨v ∅, ?_⟩
+    ext S
+    by_cases hS : S = ∅
+    · subst S
+      simp [vacuum, ket]
+    · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hS
+      have hz : phase j S * v S = 0 := by
+        rw [← annihilate_coefficient j v S hj, h j]
+        rfl
+      have hv : v S = 0 := (mul_eq_zero.mp hz).resolve_left
+        (pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num : (-1 : ℂ) ≠ 0))
+      simp [hv, vacuum, ket, hS]
+  · rintro ⟨α, rfl⟩ j
+    rw [map_smul, annihilate_vacuum, smul_zero]
+
+/-- Creator spanning extends a scalar vacuum value to the entire actual carrier. -/
+theorem eq_scalar_of_creator_commutation (A : Module.End ℂ Fock) (α : ℂ)
+    (hvac : A vacuum = α • vacuum)
+    (hc : ∀ j : ℕ, A * create j = create j * A) :
+    A = α • (1 : Module.End ℂ Fock) := by
+  apply LinearMap.ext_on_range creator_spanning
+  intro w
+  have hw : ∀ w : List ℕ,
+      A (word (w.map (fun j => (j, true))) vacuum) =
+        α • word (w.map (fun j => (j, true))) vacuum := by
+    intro w
+    induction w with
+    | nil => simpa [word] using hvac
+    | cons j w ih =>
+      have hj (v : Fock) : A (create j v) = create j (A v) :=
+        LinearMap.congr_fun (hc j) v
+      simpa only [List.map_cons, word, Module.End.mul_apply, mode, ite_true,
+        hj, ih, map_smul]
+  exact hw w
+
+end D5.S3.Quantum.Fermionic.CountableOccupationFock

+## Problem
+
+Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, and Mary Claire Simone,
+*Principal specializations of the t-chromatic symmetric function*, arXiv:2610.31785v1,
+Remark 3.11, first question:
+
+> Do (5,j,j,4,3) and (4,j,j,5,3) exhibit this phenomenon for all j?
+
+The single target is the conjunction, for every positive integer j, that the actual caterpillars
+of Definition 2.1 associated with these two compositions have unequal ordinary second principal
+specializations and equal ordinary third principal specializations. Equality and inequality are
+those of formal integer polynomials in X. Equation (2.1) uses colors 0 through k−1 and sums
+over all proper colorings; every color need not occur. The coefficient inclusion into the source's

+
+The source reports verification through j = 7. The family theorem replaces that finite range
+by every positive j, including j = 1, for the source graphs themselves. The two specialization
+comparisons form one question and one resolution.

+## Gap
+
+The source's finite verification does not establish an unbounded family. The missing uniform
+step is supplied by an identity in arbitrary repeated middle weights, after expressing the

+

+spine coloring and independent leaf color choices different from the incident spine color.

+these block weights. A part equal to one has no leaves and contributes the zeroth power one.
